description: A guitar-shaped chord generator: one polyphonic output carrying six string notes, six mute flags and the root note.

params.text: Sets the root note of the chord, one of the twelve semitones.
Chooses the chord: plain root, min, 7, Maj7, min7, 6, min6 or Sus.
Chooses open-neck voicings or bar voicings; there are no bar shapes for min6 or Sus, and those fall back to the open ones.
Chooses whether strings not played in a chord are marked muted on channels 7 to 12 or left as open strings.

inputs.text: Takes over the root note knob while a cable is here: 0V to 10V spans the twelve notes, or 1V per octave with the menu item on.
Takes over the chord knob while a cable is here: 0V to 10V spans the eight chords.
Takes over the style switch while a cable is here: below 5V chooses open voicings and 5V or more chooses bar, and the panel switch moves to follow.

outputs.text: Thirteen channels: 1 to 6 are the string notes at 1V per octave, 7 to 12 are 0V for played and 10V for muted, and 13 is the root note whether or not it is muted in the chord.

notes: There is no CV input for the mutes switch, only for the style switch.
menu: Use V/Oct Root Note Selection — reads the root note jack as 1V per octave instead of 0V to 10V; the output stays in one octave whatever octave comes in.
PianoMan Mode — puts out piano voicings in the same six-note shape: channel 1 is the root an octave down, 2 to 4 chord notes, 5 a chord note or the root up an octave, 6 the second note up.

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
